clinician.final_diagnosis: postinfectious MRI-negative transverse myelitis associated with cerebral venous thrombosis
clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her early 30s presented with severe headache, disturbed sensation on the left side of the body, and other neurological symptoms, approximately 2 weeks after a COVID-19 infection. Neurological examination revealed signs consistent with myelopathy, including a sensory deficit at T5-T6 on the left, brisk reflexes, and bilateral extensor plantar responses (E001). Brain MRI with venography showed partial thrombosis in the left transverse sinus (E002), while spinal MRI was normal, ruling out compressive myelopathy or signal abnormalities in the spinal cord (E002). Cerebrospinal fluid analysis was unremarkable, and coagulation studies including D-dimer were normal (E003). However, SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies were positive (E003), supporting a postinfectious etiology. The patient was treated with subcutaneous enoxaparin followed by oral rivaroxaban for thrombosis, and intravenous dexamethasone for myelitis (E004). A repeat MRI one week later showed persistent thrombosis and a normal spinal cord (E005). Under this therapy, the patient reported significant improvement in both headache and myelopathic symptoms (E006).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with neurological symptoms including headache and disturbed sensation on the left side of the body, following a recent COVID-19 infection.
Neurological examination showed objective signs of myelopathy, including a sensory deficit at T5-T6 on the left, brisk reflexes, and bilateral extensor plantar responses.
Spinal MRI showed no evidence of compressive myelopathy or signal abnormalities in the spinal cord, supporting 'MRI-negative' transverse myelitis.
Brain MRI with venography revealed partial thrombosis in the left transverse sinus, confirming 'cerebral venous thrombosis'.
Positive SARS-CoV-2 IgM and IgG antibodies supported the 'postinfectious' nature of the condition.
Treatment with anticoagulation and corticosteroids led to significant improvement in symptoms.
